title: The Raman Raghav Serial Murders
evidence: Bloodstained clothing and physical evidence were recovered at the time of his arrest
Fingerprint evidence connected him to the investigation
He confessed to numerous murders during police interrogation
A Special Medical Board of psychiatrists examined him repeatedly
The psychiatric board diagnosed chronic paranoid schizophrenia with auditory hallucinations
modus_operandi: Raghav primarily targeted vulnerable people living or sleeping in impoverished areas of Mumbai and attacked them with a heavy blunt weapon, often while they were asleep or otherwise defenseless.
personality_disorder: Chronic Paranoid Schizophrenia / Psychosis. A Special Medical Board concluded that Raghav was suffering from chronic paranoid schizophrenia or paraphrenia accompanied by auditory hallucinations, fixed delusions, and lack of insight into his illness.
common_traits: Lack of insight into mental illness
summary: Indian serial killer active in Mumbai during the 1960s who was linked to dozens of killings. His case is particularly significant because a Special Medical Board formally diagnosed chronic paranoid schizophrenia and found him mentally unsound, ultimately leading to his death sentence being commuted to life imprisonment.
